title: Compute brief - 14 October 2026
description: AEP plans about $4 billion for a 702 MW Bloom fuel cell plant near Cheyenne, Wyoming under a 20-year Google PPA. Fermi discloses a binding 15-year, $6.5 billion TensorWave lease for 222 MW at Project Matador, Texas. Mason County, Kentucky approves a Meta hyperscale campus. ASML says 2027 and 2028 supply will not fully meet demand. Tape: 69 confirms, 0 ticks, 0 NEW.
og_kicker: AEP 702 MW for Google; Fermi x TensorWave $6.5B; quiet tape
lede: Power and leases converted on Wednesday while prices sat still. AEP plans about $4 billion for a 702 MW Bloom Energy fuel cell plant near Cheyenne, Wyoming, selling to Google under a 20-year PPA, with construction starting in 2026 and full operation by the end of 2028. Fermi filed a fact sheet calling its TensorWave phase one lease at Project Matador, Texas binding: 15 years, $6.5 billion of contracted revenue, 222 MW total and 156 MW critical IT, delivery from Q4 2027, with AMD credit support signed a day earlier. Mason County, Kentucky approved a community benefits agreement naming Meta as developer of a hyperscale campus on more than 2,000 zoned acres. Upstream, ASML reported record Q3 sales of EUR 11.7 billion and said its planned supply for 2027 and 2028 will not fully meet customer demand. On the public silicon tape every venue returned HTTP 200 and every print held: 69 confirms, 0 ticks, 0 NEW.
